mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-52.7 to -42.7 to -34.4 to -30.7), indicating positive momentum in retail footfall recovery. This autocorrelated trend is expected to persist, driving a further increase in the mean RETAIL_REC level over the next four weeks relative to the past four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:monotonic weekly improvement in RETAIL_REC over last 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-28-day mean is equal to or lower than the last-28-day mean despite the prior monotonic 4-week uptrend.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL time has fallen steadily from 14.4 to 9.4 over four weeks, indicating reduced stay-home behavior. If RESIDENTIAL drops below 8.0, this signals a behavioral threshold where households resume discretionary out-of-home shopping and leisure, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the subsequent two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 14.4 to 9.4 over 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next two weeks even after RESIDENTIAL crosses below the 8.0 threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility rise together for two consecutive weeks, it signals synchronized resumption of commuting and in-office work, which jointly increases weekday incidental retail trips, amplifying RETAIL_REC growth beyond what either series would predict alone.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both increase week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -54.9 to -41.7 and WORKPLACES rose from -30.7 to -23.9 over 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise faster than the single-series baseline rate when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES co-move upward for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Lombardy's mobility recovery across WORKPLACES and TRANSIT reflects an active policy easing regime (zone downgrade). Under this reopening regime, continued relaxation of restrictions on commerce is expected to further lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks, but only while the region remains outside tightened-restriction tiers.
evidence_refs: fact:all mobility categories improved over the last 4 weeks
regime_hint: reopening phase under eased restriction tier
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 4 weeks while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue improving, indicating the policy-driven linkage has broken down.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility surged sharply from -37.3 to -6.9 over the past four weeks, consistent with early-season warming in February drawing people outdoors. This outdoor-activity seasonal pattern typically correlates with increased nearby retail and recreation visits within a single week as people combine errands with outdoor outings.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -37.3 to -6.9 over 4 weeks
regime_hint: seasonal transition (late winter to early spring)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the following week despite continued PARKS improvement, indicating no seasonal spillover to retail.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility drops more than 10 points week-on-week after weeks of improvement, it would signal a sudden re-tightening of regional restrictions (e.g., zone re-classification), which historically precedes sharp declines in RETAIL_REC within one week due to closures of non-essential retail.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week after prior weeks of improvement
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has been improving but remains volatile between -54.9 and -41.7
regime_hint: tightening restrictions following a zone reclassification
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise or stay flat in the week following a TRANSIT drop exceeding 10 points, rejecting the policy-tightening linkage.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in GROCERY_PHARM alongside falling RESIDENTIAL suggests households are substituting consolidated essential shopping trips for broader discretionary retail activity; when both move together, the combined effect dampens incremental RETAIL_REC growth because essential-trip saturation limits further non-essential outings.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises while RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -21.1 to -9.9 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 14.4 to 9.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC keeps rising at the same or faster rate despite concurrent GROCERY_PHARM increase and RESIDENTIAL decrease, invalidating the substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-to-late February coincides with Carnival season in Italy, a period historically associated with increased short-term retail and social activity; however, under continued pandemic-era capacity limits, this seasonal boost is expected to be muted or reversed, producing a temporary dip in RETAIL_REC relative to the ongoing recovery trend within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2021-02-15 falls within the Italian Carnival period under pandemic restrictions
regime_hint: Carnival season under pandemic capacity restrictions
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues its prior upward trajectory without any dip during the Carnival week, indicating no seasonal suppression effect.
